title: Cross-team Dependency Contracts and Escalation Simulator
creator: Priya Desai
description: Problem: Cross-functional roadmap dependencies (Engineering, Design, Security, Infra) frequently lack concrete "contracts" (commitments, SLAs, expected handoffs). When blockers occur we don’t have an objective way to quantify blast radius, run realistic escalation timelines, or test alternate mitigation paths before commitments are locked into a quarterly roadmap. This ticket proposes a lightweight productized artifact: a Dependency Contracts registry plus an Escalation Simulator. The Contracts registry captures commitment terms (owner, SLAs, soft/hard stop dates, rollback signal, test gating), and the Simulator can run deterministic scenarios (delay, partial failure, security review hold) to produce impact projections, suggested mitigations, and an escalation timeline. The goal is to give PMs and partners a shared language for commitments and a safe way to validate roadmap resiliency before approvals.
acceptance_criteria: Contracts registry schema defined and stored in Console metadata (fields: owner, contact, start_date, soft_stop, hard_stop, gating_criteria, fallback_model, rollback_steps)

Simulator UI prototype in Console that accepts a set of contracts and simulates at least three failure scenarios (5d delay, security review hold, infra capacity shortage) and outputs blast-radius metrics
Simulation outputs include: affected routes/services, customer segments impacted, estimated revenue/usage delta, required cross-team steps, and recommended escalation path
PM and two cross-functional partners (Eng lead, Design lead, Security) have validated simulator results against one real roadmap dependency case
Documentation and 2-page runbook published to Confluence with example contract templates and escalation playbook
success_metrics: Time to surface high-risk dependencies in planning reduced from 4 days to <24 hours
Number of missed cross-team commitments during release windows decreases by 30% in next quarter
>80% satisfaction from PMs in post-cycle survey on clarity of commitments and escalation paths
implementation_notes: Phase 1: schema & lightweight CRUD UI in Console (read/write via Console + API). Store contracts as Console metadata tied to initiative IDs.
Phase 2: batch simulation engine implemented as a serverless job that can run deterministic scenarios against a contract set and lookup impact signals (usage dashboards, billing SLOs, route mappings)
Phase 3: integrate with incident and escalation tooling (PagerDuty/Slack channels) to surface recommended escalation timeline and auto-notify owners when soft_stop is breached
Start with 3 pilot initiatives: Dedicated autoscaling, KV cache eviction policy, Private VPC onboarding. Use pilots to calibrate economic impact heuristics.
Privacy: simulation runs only read metadata and aggregated metrics; no PII. Security to review if runtime dashboards exposed (security_review_required=false but still notify Security for pilot).
